title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 105-108 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck is solving a matrix equation of 'loop-equation' type in the linear group over the profinite integers. He works factor by factor over the primes l in the product decomposition, so each local problem lives in GL(2, Z_l). He fixes an automorphism rho of order 3, presumably conjugation by an order-3 matrix sigma. The unknown is g = (a b; c d) with delta = det g. The equation (82) is

  g · rho(g) · rho^2(g) = 1, equivalently g·rho(g) = rho^2(g^{-1}).

He has already computed g·rho(g) = (P Q; R S) in (81) and rho^2(g^{-1}) in (77). He compares entries. The (1,1) entries give P = (a+b)(c+d-b) = (a+b)/delta. Since Z_l is a domain, he splits into two cases.

Case 1: a+b ≠ 0.
- Then c+d-b = 1/delta, which is (83).
- Given (83), the remaining identities are Q = (c+d-(a+b))/delta = 1/delta^2 - a/delta, R = b/delta, and S = (d-b)/delta = 1/delta^2 - c/delta.
- These are equivalent to delta^3 = 1, which is (84). He notes this was necessary a priori: taking determinants gives det(g)^3 = 1, because rho preserves the determinant.
- A marginal NB adds that (83) and (84) are sufficient for (82) even without assuming a+b ≠ 0.

Case 2: a+b = 0.
- Then a = -b and det g = -b(c+d) = delta, so d = -delta/b - c.
- This gives P = 0, Q = -b^2, R = delta^2/b^2, S = delta + c(delta/b + b).
- Also rho^2(g^{-1}) = (0, -1/b; b/delta, -(1/delta)(delta/b + b + c)).
- Equating entries gives (87):
  - (87a) b^3 = delta^3 = 1;
  - (87b) c((b delta)^2 + b delta + 1) + (delta^2 + b^2 delta + b) = 0.

The next page splits further on whether b·delta = 1 or b·delta is a primitive cube root of unity.

Modern viewpoint: rho(g) = sigma g sigma^{-1} with sigma^3 = 1. Then g·rho(g)·rho^2(g) = (g sigma)^3 sigma^{-3} = (g sigma)^3. So (82) just says h = g·sigma has order dividing 3, and the solution set is {h sigma^{-1} : h^3 = 1}. Equivalently it is the set of 1-cocycles of Z/3 acting on GL(2, Z_l) through rho. Grothendieck instead parametrises this variety by brute-force coordinates. Its case split corresponds to the possible characteristic polynomials of h:
- (x - zeta)(x - zeta') with zeta, zeta' cube roots of unity;
- the non-trivial cube roots of unity exist in Z_l only when l ≡ 1 mod 3.
errors: No genuine mathematical error found on this page. (87) can be re-derived from the stated P, Q, R, S and rho^2(g^{-1}). Equating the (2,2) entries and multiplying by b·delta gives c(delta^2 + b^2 delta + b) + (b delta^2 + delta + b^2) = 0. Multiplying by b^2 and using b^3 = 1 recovers exactly Grothendieck's form (87b).

The marginal NB claims sufficiency 'independently of a+b ≠ 0', and possibly something about necessity when a+b = 0. Its wording is only partly legible, and the necessity part is not justified on the page: when a+b = 0, P = 0 holds automatically, so c+d-b = 1/delta is not forced.

ideas.what: Solving the twisted cube/cocycle equation g·rho(g)·rho^2(g) = 1 in GL(2, Z_l), for an order-3 automorphism rho, prime by prime via the product decomposition over l
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian 1-cocycles of Z/3 with values in GL_2 (equivalently, elements of order 3 in the coset GL_2·sigma); linearised abelian/SL_2 shadow of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller 3-cycle relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: The 3-cycle relation in GT is due to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara; studying images of GT-type equations in SL_2(Z-hat) appears in work of Lochak, Schneps and others
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Using the determinant to see a priori that det(g)^3 = 1

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine coordinate computation of the solution set of a cocycle-type equation in GL_2(Z_l). It is correct but elementary, and it is equivalent to classifying order-3 elements in a coset. Its interest lies only in the GT/'équation des lacets' context, which is better documented elsewhere in the manuscript.
transcription_corrections: The formula for Q reads Q = (c+d-(a+b))/delta (= 1/delta^2 - a/delta). The '(a+b)' is overwritten rather than deleted, and the stray 'a' is a correction artifact.

The margin NB (written diagonally) reads approximately: 'NB Les conditions c+d-b = 1/delta, delta^3 = 1 sont suffisantes (indépendamment de la condition a+b ≠ 0) pour la validité de (82); si a+b = 0 elles sont nécessaires [?] ... cas 3° ci-dessous' (partly illegible).
The opening line reads 'Moyennant (83), on vérifie que les formules (82), — où il reste à vérifier'.
